movie.overview: Chris Carter’s Vrach Frankenshteyn cut features the same core plot as the original theatrical release—with Mulder and Scully pulled back into the FBI by a disgraced, psychic priest (Father Joe) to investigate the kidnapping of women. However, this version restores Carter's original, grislier medical gore and darker tone

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: In Chris Carter's darker cut, former FBI agents Fox Mulder and Dana Scully reunite to investigate a series of gruesome kidnappings connected to an organ-harvesting operation and a disgraced, psychic priest.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: When an FBI agent goes missing, the bureau seeks out Dana Scully to help persuade Fox Mulder to consult on the case. Guided by the disturbing visions of Father Joe, a convicted pedophile priest claiming psychic insights, Mulder and Scully uncover a horrifying medical experiment taking place in the frozen wilderness. As Scully wrestles with her faith and medical ethics in a separate case involving a terminally ill boy, Mulder pursues the grotesque truth behind the missing women. Restoring Carter's original vision, this version emphasizes the story's visceral medical horror and heavy emotional weight.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Years after leaving the FBI, Dana Scully works as a physician at a Catholic hospital, while Fox Mulder lives as a recluse continuing his research into the paranormal. The FBI requests Scully's assistance to locate Mulder after an agent is abducted in Virginia, offering to drop all past charges against him in exchange for his expertise. They are brought into the investigation by Father Joseph Crissman, a disgraced priest who experiences agonizing, supernatural visions of the crimes. Father Joe leads the agents and FBI team to a severed arm buried in the snow, triggering a desperate hunt for the missing women. As the investigation deepens, Mulder identifies a sinister pattern involving body parts and organ transplantation. Meanwhile, Scully faces a personal dilemma as she tries to save a young patient with an incurable disease using experimental stem-cell therapies, drawing parallels to the rogue medical procedures being conducted by the kidnappers. The trail leads to a remote organ-harvesting ring run by a radical scientist attempting human head transplants to prolong his dying lover's life. Mulder pursues the suspects to an isolated compound where the grislier elements of the human experimentation are laid bare. With Scully arriving in time to assist, they defeat the perpetrators and rescue the surviving victim, leaving Mulder and Scully to confront their own beliefs, relationship, and the fragile nature of hope.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: The X-Files: I Want to Believe – Vrach Frankenshteyn presents a darker, more visceral realization of Chris Carter's 2008 feature film. Disconnected from the overarching alien mythology of the series, the story functions as a standalone psychological thriller and medical horror. Former FBI agent Dana Scully, now a dedicated hospital doctor, is approached by her former employers to trace her reclusive partner, Fox Mulder. The FBI needs Mulder's unconventional mind to evaluate the claims of Father Joe, a former priest claiming to receive divine visions regarding a string of local abductions. Despite Scully's intense skepticism toward the disgraced priest, Mulder follows Father Joe's cryptic clues, unearthing a terrifying crime network operating in the shadows of the winter landscape. The narrative contrasts Mulder's relentless search for truth against Scully's internal moral struggle over life-prolonging medical treatments, creating a thematic parallel between faith, ethics, and human survival. This cut emphasizes the body-horror elements of rogue transplantation procedures while exploring the complex dynamic between two iconic investigators forced to confront darkness both external and within.
